# @stackline/deepmerge

Drop-in replacement for deepmerge 4. Same results as deepmerge 4.3.1, with
CVE-2026-93753 fixed, circular references supported, and opt-in hardening,
Map and Set merging, and array strategies. Zero runtime dependencies.

## Canonical resources

- Documentation: https://alexandro.net/docs/vanilla/deepmerge/
- Compatibility contract: https://alexandro.net/docs/vanilla/deepmerge/guides/compatibility.md
- Upstream issue review: https://alexandro.net/docs/vanilla/deepmerge/guides/upstream.md
- Portfolio catalog: https://alexandro.net/docs/open-source/

- Full LLM reference: https://alexandro.net/docs/vanilla/deepmerge/llms-full.txt

## Install

Drop-in alias: npm install deepmerge@npm:@stackline/deepmerge

Direct: npm install @stackline/deepmerge

## Core contract

- Without options, results match deepmerge 4.3.1: values, key order,
  prototypes, descriptors, and independent copies.
- Arrays concatenate by default; inputs are never mutated.
- __proto__ is dropped at every depth (CVE-2026-93753).
- constructor and prototype follow deepmerge 4 unless unsafeKeys is "strict".
- Cycles are reproduced instead of overflowing the stack.
- strict(target, source) adds strict keys, throwing, and depth and key limits.
- Opt-in: createDeepmerge, skipUndefined, mergeCollections, customMergeScope,
  isPlainMergeableObject, overwriteArrays, mergeArraysByIndex,
  mergeArraysByKey, concatUniqueArrays.
- ESM, callable CommonJS, browser global, and TypeScript are supported.
